title: Number systems on the number line

widget.instructions: Drag the ends of a piece, or use the buttons below the line.

steps.text: Every real number has a place on the number line. Integers sit at the whole-number marks.
Rational numbers are fractions p ÷ q of integers, like ½ or −3/4: they fill in between the integers.
Some numbers, like √2 ≈ 1.414…, can't be written as a fraction: they are irrational, but they still have a place on the line.
Distance on the line is always positive: from −3 to 2 is 2 − (−3) = 5.
Think of a number as a walk from 0: positive steps go right, negative steps go left.
The distance between two numbers is how far you walk from one to the other, whatever the direction.

recap.text: Recap: integers, rationals (fractions) and irrationals (like √2) all sit on the real number line; distance = larger − smaller.

accessibility.nonDragAlternative: Use the buttons below the number line; the description below it gives every position.
